standard_prerequisites: The notion of quasi-inverse of a function: a triple consisting of a function in the reverse direction and two homotopies, defined by the retained context.

The notion of equivalence of types as an improved, structure-respecting predicate on functions, written f in the equivalence type from A to B; the author's definition and its motivation are background for this card.
Homotopies between functions and identity functions on types.
core_obligations: Prove reflexivity: the identity function on any type is an equivalence, being its own quasi-inverse.
Prove inversion: if f is an equivalence from A to B with quasi-inverse g, then g is an equivalence from B to A, with f as a quasi-inverse.

Prove composition: if f from A to B and g from B to C are equivalences with quasi-inverses, then the composite g after f is an equivalence from A to C, the composite of the quasi-inverses being its quasi-inverse.
proof_roadmap: Reflexivity: the identity function is its own quasi-inverse with the homotopies both given by reflexivity, so it is an equivalence.
Inversion: if f has quasi-inverse g, then f is also a quasi-inverse of g, so g is an equivalence in the reverse direction.

Composition: given quasi-inverses of f and of g, verify directly that the composite of the two quasi-inverses is a quasi-inverse of the composite: for any a the needed identification follows by cancelling the inner pair g inverse with g and then f inverse with f; the mirrored verification is symmetric.
Conclude that equivalence of types is an equivalence relation on the universe: reflexive, symmetric (by inversion), and transitive (by composition).
difficulty_reason: Three short quasi-inverse verifications; the only care point is composing the homotopies in the correct order in the transitivity case.
